title: Client-side privacy tags + localization probe
content:
Context / motivation:
- Working through a lightweight client-side tagging approach so apps can: 1) declare which text segments are private/sensitive, 2) mark locale/context for local-only transformations, and 3) provide hints to the server-side routing/transformations to avoid sending private content upstream when the tenant uses Private deployment or offline-first features.
- Goal: minimal change to SDK surface, backwards compatible default (no-op if not used), opt-in privacy modes for both hosted and private deployments.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full DLP pipeline — no plans here to run deep pattern matching or regex-based scrubbing on the client. Focus is metadata + lightweight client transforms (redaction placeholders, local translations).

Open questions:
- How explicit should the client be about what gets kept local vs allowed to be sent? (explicit allow-list vs explicit deny-list)
- How do we version tag semantics so old clients talking to new servers don’t leak semantics? (policy: server should ignore unknown tags)
- UX: should tags be attached to spans, full messages, or both? (preference: spans for fine-grained control)

Design sketch — API surface (JS client pseudocode):

// high level usage
const ctx = client.createContext({ tenant: 'acme', privacyMode: 'opt-in' });
const msg = ctx.message('compose');
msg.addSpan('user_text', { text: 'My SSN is 123-45-6789', tags: ['sensitive.personal_identifiers'] });
msg.addSpan('system_hint', { text: 'translate:fr', tags: ['localization.hint'] });
await ctx.send(msg);

Notes on the above:
- createContext opts: privacyMode: 'off' | 'opt-in' | 'strict' where 'strict' blocks any span tagged with sensitivity above level X from being sent to hosted endpoints.
- addSpan shape: { id: string, text: string, tags?: string[], meta?: { locale?: string, checksum?: string } }

JSON example payload sent over the wire (server-compatible):
{
  "message_id": "m-abc-123",
  "spans": [
    {"id":"s1","text":"My SSN is [redacted]","tags":["sensitive.personal_identifiers"],"meta":{"redacted":true}},
    {"id":"s2","text":"translate:fr","tags":["localization.hint"],"meta":{"locale":"en"}}
  ],
  "client_tags_version": "v1"
}

Client-side transform rules (sketch):
- If privacyMode == 'strict' and span.tag matches sensitive.* => do not include original text, replace with redaction token and set meta.redacted=true.
- If privacyMode == 'opt-in' and span.tag is in client.allowlist => include full text, else redact. Allowlist managed by client config or tenant policy.
- localization.hint spans: if offline/localization enabled -> perform local translate() and replace text before sending; include meta.translated=true

Server expectations and compatibility:
- Server must accept 'redaction token' and meta.redacted markers; server should avoid treating redacted placeholders as ground truth (e.g., avoid generating output that uses placeholder as real content).
- Unknown tags: server must ignore unknown tags (forward compatibility).
- Servers in Private deployments may opt into a stricter policy where any sensitive.* tags cause request to be refused with 403 unless endpoint is private.

Policy and policy distribution:
- Policy documents (allowlist/denylist, sensitivity levels) will be hosted in tenant config.
- SDK will cache policy & offer a small embedded policy editor in Console for quick config.
- Versioning: client_tags_version field included in payload; server may annotate response with accepted_policy_version.

Lightweight local policy DSL (informal):
- rule: sensitive.personal_identifiers -> action: redact if privacyMode in [opt-in,strict] && not in explicitAllow
- rule: localization.* -> action: local_transform if local_caps.translate==true

Edge cases / examples:
- User attaches an image with embedded text (OCR needed): client can tag attachment span as sensitive.image_text but not perform OCR locally by default. If client enables local OCR (cost/perf), it can produce spans that are treated same as other spans.
- Multi-locale conversations: per-span meta.locale used to inform local transforms; if missing, use context locale.

Telemetry / observability notes:
- Track counts: spans_sent, spans_redacted, local_transforms_applied, local_policy_hits.
- Telemetry must never include original text of redacted spans. Only counters and policy decision codes.

Implementation plan (phased):
1) v0: basic tagging API + redaction tokenging in SDK, server ignore tags. (2 week spike)
2) v1: add privacyMode, local transforms for localization hints, client policy fetch/caching, telemetry counters. (4-6 weeks)
3) v2: policy editor in Console + tenant-level strict enforcement + versioning guarantees. (8-12 weeks)

TODOs:
- [ ] write unit tests for span-level redaction
- [ ] add e2e smoke with Private deployment: ensure strict mode blocks hosted requests
- [ ] finalize tag taxonomy (proposal draft to Confluence)
- [ ] check legal for required disclosures when redacting PII on client

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments:
- Could we compress span metadata into a compact bitfield for low-bandwidth mobile clients? 
- Consider optional signed-hash of original span stored locally so client can restore context if user re-authorizes developer to send real content to server (audit trail)
- If server later requests original span (e.g., user initiates human-review flow), SDK could prompt user to re-send with explicit consent flow.

Sketch diagram (ASCII) for runtime flow:

[App UI] -> [SDK: tag spans / apply policy] -> (if local_transform) [local worker] -> [SDK: prepare payload w/ redactions] -> [Network] -> [Server: route by tenant/policy]
                                |
                                +-> [Local store: encrypted span cache] (optional)

Final thoughts:
- Keep default behavior conservative (no tagging behavior unless app uses new API).
- Prioritize developer ergonomics: small API surface, clear migration path, helpful console tools to inspect policy.
- Implementation should favor being auditable and observable without exposing content.

References / related notes:
- related: airgap-private-deploy-operator-runbook-sketch.json (drive: users) — handling of private routes
- related: ephemeral-client-policy-dsl-sketch.json (drive: users)

End of probe (very rough).
